```text
Peak Poker Performance

ance is determined by how committed and passionate you are about your

Summary
As you can tell, achieving peak performance is a long-term process. There
will be many trials and tribulations and twists and turns along the way.
Besides that, performing at our best is not a one-time thing. If you want
to achieve more consistent results, you have to be motivated to keep
working at it. Passion is the factor that drives the motivation engine. If
you put all of your passion into becoming the best poker player you can
be, you have a shot at becoming one of the best players in the world.
    Of course, not everything will always go smoothly. You can do every-
thing well and still lose a high percentage of the time. Even the most win-
ning poker players spend a great deal of time losing hands and sessions.
Having a vision or purpose is important to maintaining long-term motiva-
tion, and it can help you stay in the game even when things are not going
well. If you are clear enough on your purpose and it is important enough
to you, no obstacle will get in your way. Focus on your “why” and the
“how” will become more evident. If you are willing to devote yourself to
becoming the best poker player you can be, you’ll do whatever it takes to
overcome setbacks, hurdles, variance, and doubts. I am convinced that
following the suggestions in this book will put you on the path to becom-
ing better and more successful at poker. The secret is in learning to love
the process of becoming better. If you focus on your vision and are pas-
sionate about the game, peak performance is within reach.

Chapter Highlights
     ♠ It is critical to have some sort of deeper “why” for your pursuits
        than simply monetary goals. What is your “why?”
     ♠ Mastery is a personal journey.
     ♠ Develop a growth mindset to aid in achieving all that you want to
        accomplish.
```

```text
Jonathan’s Comments
After my first session of playing poker as a 17-year-old kid for tiny
stakes in the back room of a comic book store, I knew I wanted to get
good at the game. The idea that I could use my brain to outplay someone
at a card game for significant money ($10 at the time!) was astounding
to me. I instantly dropped everything else I did for fun and spent every
free second reading about poker. At that point in time, no training sites
existed and No-Limit Hold’Em was the second most popular form of
poker, behind Limit Hold’Em. I took to learning Limit by devouring every
book I could find.
   After I felt confident I had studied enough to become a competent
player – I had read every book in print on poker (not just on Limit
Hold’Em) – I deposited $50 into an online poker site. Fortunately, my
competitors had not studied at all. I spent all of my free moments playing
and eventually grew my bankroll to over $15,000 within a year.
   At that point, Limit Hold’Em started getting tougher, so I decided to
try No-Limit Hold’Em SnGs, which I heard were a very mathematical
game. I downloaded a now-defunct program called Sit N’ Go Power Tools
and analyzed every hand I played. Each day, I spent six hours playing and
four hours studying. Whenever I went on a downswing, I would take a day
off from playing and study the entire time instead. By learning the SnG
formula, I quickly became one of the best in the world at that game.
```

```text
craft.

poker), I recently set a clearly defined goal to be one of the top 10 tour-

18 months. To put things into perspective, I am currently ranked #65.
The highest I have ever been was #25. This goal seems fairly difficult to
achieve, but I think it is within reach. In order to achieve this goal, I will
have to spend significant time studying various aspects of the game and
put in lots of volume. Of course, I will also have to win some tournaments,
and winning is quite luck based. Since there is a large luck component in-
volved, I recognize that failure is a likely outcome and will not be too dis-
```

```text
resolutions don’t even last the month of January. Why do you suppose so
many people fail to keep their resolutions?

what needs to be done to get the results we are after, but quite another
to do those things daily. You are probably well aware that eating better
```

```text
Peak Poker Performance

eat better and exercise more? As a general rule, we don’t fail to keep our
resolutions because we lack knowledge about why they would be good
for us. We fail because we don’t know how to consistently do what is re-
quired to make reaching our goals a habit. Excellence is not something
you do once in a while; it’s what you do repeatedly and consistently. Play-
ers, who do reach their goals in poker (or in life generally), endeavor con-
sistently to do things that make them more successful. This is so impor-
tant that I want to repeat it. The difference between those who are suc-
cessful and those who are not is not due to a difference in intelligence or
talent but because of the habits that they keep. Habits are the corner-
stone of peak performance.
    Obviously, it is not an easy thing to get the habit-ball rolling. If it was,
everyone would be successful! You have to learn how to establish habits
and routines that guarantee your success. Relying on your intention to
behave in a beneficial way rarely works out. What does work is to put
these behaviors on autopilot by using your limited willpower to install
them as habits. Once a behavior is an ingrained habit, we will do it no
matter what. Habits allow us to translate what we know we should do
into things we actually do. Let’s take a deeper look into how it all works.
    A habit is simply a recurrent, often unconscious, pattern of behavior
acquired through frequent repetition. In recent years, the subject of hab-
its has become quite popular in psychological circles. Several bestsellers
have been written on the topic and, more importantly, hundreds of stud-
ies have been conducted. There is a good reason why habits are garnering
so much attention. They are extremely important to your success in the
poker world and in life generally because greatness is formed by good
habits. As Aristotle once said, “We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence,
then, is not an act, but a habit.”
    Hal Elrod, author of The Miracle Morning says, “Considering that our
habits create our life, there is arguably no single skill that is more impor-
tant for you to learn and master than controlling your habits” (2014). He
concludes that identifying, implementing, and maintaining the habits nec-
essary for creating the life you want, while letting go of negative habits, is
```

```text
                                                  Create Winning Habits

the key ingredient to living up to our fullest potential.
   Another author, Og Mandino said, “The only difference between those
who have failed and those who have succeeded lies in the difference of
their habits. Good habits are the key to all success. Bad habits are the
unlocked door to failure.” Mandino was an American author who sold over
50 million copies of his books, so he knows something about being suc-
cessful. He advised that we “form good habits and become their slave.”
   Whether you know it or not, many (if not most) of the actions you
take and the thoughts you think each day are simply habits. Even procras-
tination is a habit. Many scientists suggest that up to 50% of all the ac-
tions we take on any given day are based on habit. Habitual behavior is
super important because those repetitions do add up. For example, if you
make it a habit to write 1,000 words a day, at the end of one year you
will have written the equivalent of seven novels! Because of this, it makes
sense to orchestrate your habits in such a way that they help you achieve
what you want. Understanding more about how to shape and mold your
habits is probably the single most efficient and effective route to improv-
ing your overall results and to performing at your peak.
   Knowing the science behind habit formation can be extremely useful
because there are a myriad of ways you can use the information to en-
hance your game. Habits act as mental shortcuts. If you want to use your
brain more efficiently and make the most of the prefrontal cortex’s lim-
ited mental processing capabilities, then managing your habits is the way
to go.
   As you will see, putting certain behaviors on autopilot frees up your
brain’s processing power for more important things – like maintaining
good self-discipline while you are playing. This is because every time we
make a decision or think through a problem, we are depleting some of our
precious willpower. Habitual behaviors (and thoughts for that matter) do
not require any willpower or motivation. If you are after optimization,
your goal should be to build as many good habits as possible while avoid-
ing bad ones.
```
